answer: LIST t, sl, sies FROM Fund f has FundTickersym t AND ALSO has FundShortlabel sl AND ALSO has FundYieldrate y AND ALSO has FundExpensenet e AND ALSO is of BondAllocation [has BondRating has BondRatingRatekey rk] has BondAllocationAllocationpct p AND ALSO THE SUM OF p GROUPED BY t AS hq AND ALSO (y / e) * hq AS sies WHERE rk < 4 AND y / e > 15 AND hq > 0.6 ORDERED WITH sies DESCENDING
note: The 'premier rank' column could NOT be expressed. ConQuer has no window function and no correlated comparison against a bound value: '!x' only works inside a denotation (has T: !x), so 'count of premier funds scoring above this one' is unwritable, and there is no self-join between two Funds. The rows come back in rank order, so the rank is the row position, but it is not a column. Everything else is exact: high-quality credit = BondRating ratekeys 1-3 (us_government, aaa, aa), allocations are fractions so the threshold is 0.6, YTER = yieldrate/expensenet > 15, SIES = YTER * that allocation. 25 funds qualify.

answer: LIST if(flag = 0, 'Transparent', 'Opaque'), n, round(m, 4) FROM Fund f OPTIONALLY has FundPeRatio pe AND ALSO OPTIONALLY is of Performance OPTIONALLY has PerformanceR1y r AND ALSO (abs(pe) - abs(pe)) AS flag AND ALSO THE DISTINCT COUNT OF f GROUPED BY flag AS n AND ALSO THE AVERAGE r GROUPED BY flag AS m
note: The MEDIAN could not be expressed: ConQuer offers only COUNT/DISTINCT COUNT/SUM/AVERAGE/MINIMUM/MAXIMUM, no median or percentile, and no per-group ordering, so this query reports the AVERAGE 1-year return in its place (Transparent 0.4485, Opaque 0.1638). The true medians, obtained separately with ORDERED WITH ... THE FIRST n AFTER m, are Transparent 0.4097 (n=1243 with a return) and Opaque 0.0578 (n=670, mean of the two middle values). Group counts are right: Transparent 1493, Opaque 813. Two workarounds were needed: there is no IS NULL, so presence is tested as abs(pe)-abs(pe) being 0 rather than NULL; and grouping directly by an if(...) with string literals hits a compiler bug (bind-parameter count mismatch when the CASE is repeated in GROUP BY), so the group key is the literal-free flag and the labels are applied in the projection. Only P/E is tested because every fund with a P/E also has a P/B (1493 of each, 1493 with both), making the two-part test redundant here.

answer: LIST t, amv, round((THE COUNT OF Fund [is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricAvgreturn3y a2] [is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricVolatility3y v2] [is of Performance has PerformanceBenchr3y b2] [has FundExpensenet e2] [has FundBenchmarkexp x2] WHERE (a2 - b2) / v2 - (e2 - x2) * 10 > 0) * 100 / (THE COUNT OF Fund [is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricAvgreturn3y a3] [is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricVolatility3y v3] [is of Performance has PerformanceBenchr3y b3] [has FundExpensenet e3] [has FundBenchmarkexp x3]), 4) FROM Fund has FundTickersym t AND ALSO is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricAvgreturn3y ar AND ALSO is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricVolatility3y v AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformanceBenchr3y br AND ALSO has FundExpensenet en AND ALSO has FundBenchmarkexp be AND ALSO round((ar - br) / v - (en - be) * 10, 4) AS amv ORDERED WITH amv DESCENDING THE FIRST 10
note: AMV = IR - (relative expense * 10); IR = (RiskMetricAvgreturn3y - PerformanceBenchr3y) / RiskMetricVolatility3y. Ambiguity: 'fund's 3-year average return' could be RiskMetricAvgreturn3y or PerformanceR3y; I used avg_return_3y because the wording says 'average return', even though its scale (-11.5..8.3) does not match the fractional benchmark return. The scalar percentage is carried as a third column repeated on all 10 rows (93.9484%), denominator = the 1008 funds for which AMV is computable. Parentheses around the two COUNT subqueries are essential or the '*100/' is swallowed into the subquery's WHERE.

answer: THE DISTINCT COUNT OF Fund [is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricAlpha5y a] [is of Holding has HoldingPct p] WHERE a > 0 AND p > 0.08
note: Focused Alpha Leader = Alpha Generator (5y alpha > 0) and High-Conviction Portfolio (largest holding > 8%). The Performance top-weight column exists in the model but is entirely NULL, so the largest-holding weight had to come from Holding.HoldingPct (stored as a fraction, so 8% = 0.08). A fund qualifies iff some holding exceeds 0.08, which is the same as its rank-1 holding exceeding it; both formulations returned 144. DISTINCT COUNT is required because the Holding step fans out.

answer: round(THE AVERAGE c IN (Fund is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricAvgreturn3y ar AND ALSO is of RiskMetric has RiskMetricVolatility3y v AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformanceBenchr3y br AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformancePositiveyears py AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformanceNegativeyears ny AND ALSO ((ar - br) / v) * (py / (py + ny)) AS c), 2)
note: CAIR = IR * consistency/100, so the /100 and the *100 in the consistency definition cancel to py/(py+ny). Same IR ambiguity as question 12 (avg_return_3y vs r3y as the fund's 3-year return). Unrounded value 0.04561, so the 2-decimal answer 0.05 is sensitive to that choice: using PerformanceR3y instead would round to 0.00. No fund has py+ny = 0, so no divide-by-zero guard was needed.

answer: LIST y, cur, prev, chg FROM Fund [has FundTickersym: 'AADR'] is of AnnualReturn [has AnnualReturnCalendaryear y] [has AnnualReturnFundperf fp] has AnnualReturnCategoryperf cp AND ALSO is of AnnualReturn [has AnnualReturnCalendaryear y2] [has AnnualReturnFundperf fp2] has AnnualReturnCategoryperf cp2 AND ALSO (fp - cp) AS cur AND ALSO (fp2 - cp2) AS prev AND ALSO (fp - cp) - (fp2 - cp2) AS chg WHERE y2 = y - 1 ORDERED WITH y ASCENDING
note: There is no LAG, so the previous year is a self-join of AnnualReturn through Fund with WHERE y2 = y - 1. Consequence: the earliest year (2011) is dropped, where a LAG-based answer would show it with a NULL previous outperformance; the query returns 2012-2015. I could not keep it: OPTIONALLY does not push the y2 = y-1 test into the join, a denotation cannot carry arithmetic ([has ...Calendaryear: !y - 1] does not parse), and starting the path at AnnualReturn instead of Fund makes the compiler emit a self-join on the wrong column (annual3.tickersym) and fail.

answer: LIST c, n, slope, r2 FROM RiskMetric r has RiskMetricAlpha3y y AND ALSO has Fund has Category has CategoryCatref c AND ALSO has Fund has FundTurnoverratio x AND ALSO (x * y) AS xy AND ALSO (x * x) AS xx AND ALSO (y * y) AS yy AND ALSO THE COUNT OF r GROUPED BY c AS n AND ALSO THE SUM OF x GROUPED BY c AS sx AND ALSO THE SUM OF y GROUPED BY c AS sy AND ALSO THE SUM OF xy GROUPED BY c AS sxy AND ALSO THE SUM OF xx GROUPED BY c AS sxx AND ALSO THE SUM OF yy GROUPED BY c AS syy AND ALSO round((n * sxy - sx * sy) / (n * sxx - sx * sx), 4) AS slope AND ALSO round((n * sxy - sx * sy) * (n * sxy - sx * sy) / ((n * sxx - sx * sx) * (n * syy - sy * sy)), 4) AS r2 WHERE n > 25 ORDERED WITH slope DESCENDING THE FIRST 100
note: OLS slope and R-squared built by hand from grouped sums (no regression aggregate in the language). Two things forced the shape: the query must start at RiskMetric, because Fund->RiskMetric is not declared functional and the compiler refuses a COUNT that the path multiplies; and the cross-products x*y, x*x, y*y must be bound with AS before they can be summed. 'productclass' is emitted as CategoryCatref, the value actually stored on the fund (Fund has Category via 'productclass'); if the expected output is the category name it would be CategoryClasstype instead. Only 9 categories have more than 25 funds with both alpha and turnover, so the 'top 100' limit never bites.

answer: LIST t, sl, pp FROM Fund has FundTickersym t AND ALSO has FundShortlabel sl AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformanceLow52w lo AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformanceHigh52w hi AND ALSO is of Performance has PerformanceLowdelta ld AND ALSO has FundTurnoverratio tr AND ALSO has FundExpensenet en AND ALSO has FundBenchmarkexp be AND ALSO round(ld / (hi - lo) * 100, 8) AS pp WHERE pp < 25 AND tr < 0.3 AND en - be < 0 ORDERED WITH pp ASCENDING THE FIRST 100
note: There is no 'recent price' attribute anywhere in the model; it has to be reconstructed as low52w + lowdelta (verified: it equals high52w + highdelta on every row). Price position therefore simplifies to lowdelta/(high52w-low52w)*100. Turnover is a fraction, so the low-turnover test is < 0.3. 51 funds qualify, fewer than the requested 100.
